OCTOBER 2026 POWER RATE ADVISORY
Negros Power’s average residential electricity rate for October 2026 is ₱14.2691 per kWh, a slight increase of ₱0.0204 per kWh from last month’s rate of ₱14.2487 per kWh.
 Why did electricity rates increase slightly?
Despite the significant increase in electricity prices in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM), Negros Power’s staggered payment scheme helped reduce the immediate impact on consumers. As a result, the overall increase in the residential electricity rate remained minimal.
 Higher WESM Rate, Lower Generation Charge
The WESM rate increased from ₱9.8812/kWh to ₱13.6087/kWh, mainly due to higher electricity demand and the temporary unavailability of several power plants. This contributed to Yellow and Red Alerts in the Luzon and Visayas grids, as available power supply became tighter.
To help protect consumers from the full impact of these higher electricity costs, Negros Power implemented a staggered payment scheme. Instead of collecting the entire increase at once, only a portion will be charged this month, while the remaining amount will be spread over the next five months.
With this arrangement, the generation charge decreased by ₱0.5050/kWh for October, helping cushion the impact of higher WESM prices.
 Slight Increase in Transmission Charges
Transmission charges increased by ₱0.1411/kWh, mainly due to slight increases in transmission and ancillary services for the reserve market.
 Adjustment in Universal Charge for Missionary Electrification (UCME)
The UCME rate increased by ₱0.0634/kWh, following the implementation of the new rate of ₱0.3397/kWh under the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) Order dated October 2, 2026. This adjustment is related to the National Power Corporation’s UCME.
October 2026 Average Electricity Rate
Residential (RES): Php 14.2691/kWh 
Low Voltage (LV): Php 14.2697/kWh
High Voltage (HV): Php 13.1505/kWh
In summary, although electricity prices in the WESM rose significantly, Negros Power’s staggered payment scheme helped lessen the immediate impact on consumers. Together with adjustments in transmission charges and the UCME rate, these changes resulted in only a slight increase of ₱0.0204/kWh in the average residential electricity rate for October 2026.
